chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAlī ibn al-Sindī, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who prayed one rakʿah with tayammum, then a man came carrying two waterskins of water. He said: He cuts off the prayer, performs wudu (ablution), then builds upon the one rakʿah.

The proper way regarding this report is that we carry it upon one who, after praying one rakʿah, had an occurrence that invalidates wudu (ablution) forgetfully; then it is obligatory upon him to perform wudu (ablution) and build on the prayer. But if he had not invalidated it, then turning away would not have been obligatory for him; rather, he would have had to continue in his prayer.

And it is not possible to say regarding this report what we said regarding others, namely that wudu (ablution) is only obligatory upon him because he entered it before the end of the time; for if that were so, then it would not be permissible for him to build on the prayer, and restarting would have been obligatory upon him. What indicates the permissibility of what we have said is when he invalidates it forgetfully.

key_terms.الِاسْتِئْنَافُ: restarting the prayer from the beginning
key_terms.الِانْصِرَافُ: turning away from and discontinuing the prayer
key_terms.تَيَمُّمٍ: dry ablution used in place of wudu (ablution) when water is unavailable
key_terms.يَبْنِيَ: he resumes and continues based on what has already been performed

ai.seo_question: If someone starts salat with tayammum and then finds water, should he break the prayer and perform wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of one who begins salat with tayammum and then water becomes available. The text explains that the report is to be understood as applying to a case where the person had a forgetful invalidation of wudu (ablution), so he performs wudu (ablution) and resumes from what he had completed. Otherwise, if no nullifying event occurred, he should continue the prayer and not break it.
